classification.difficultyReason: Apply the horizontal line test to nine supplied graphs.

content.prompt: For each graph, decide whether the inverse will be a function.

spec.description: Increasing straight line through the origin, arrowed at both ends; positive axis ends arrowed and labelled.
spec.mathematics: Schematic line with positive slope. No numerical scale or equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: Every horizontal line meets the graph at most once, so the inverse is a function.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with vertex at the origin, symmetric about the vertical axis, arrowed at both upper ends.
spec.mathematics: Schematic parabola; plotting coordinates are internal and do not supply a numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: A horizontal line above the vertex meets the graph twice. The graph fails the horizontal line test, so the inverse is not a function.

spec.description: Increasing concave-up right-hand branch beginning at the origin, with only its upper end arrowed.
spec.mathematics: Preserves the displayed restricted branch without adding a left-hand branch or endpoint marker. No equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: On the displayed branch, every horizontal line meets the graph at most once, so the inverse is a function.

spec.description: Increasing exponential-shaped graph above the horizontal axis, approaching it on the left and rising steeply on the right; arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Schematic exponential curve with a positive vertical-axis intercept. No numerical scale or equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: Every horizontal line meets the increasing graph at most once, so the inverse is a function.

spec.description: V-shaped graph with vertex at the origin, two upward arrowed rays and symmetry about the vertical axis.
spec.mathematics: Schematic absolute-value shape with no numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: A horizontal line above the vertex meets both rays. The graph fails the horizontal line test, so the inverse is not a function.

spec.description: Increasing concave-down root-shaped curve starting on the positive horizontal axis to the right of the origin; right end arrowed.
spec.mathematics: Preserves the unmarked starting endpoint and positive horizontal shift. No equation or numerical shift is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: Every horizontal line meets the displayed increasing curve at most once, so the inverse is a function.

spec.description: Upper semicircle with horizontal-axis endpoints labelled −1 and 1, symmetric about the vertical axis; no curve arrows or endpoint markers.
spec.mathematics: Circular upper arc spanning the supplied horizontal endpoints. No vertical numerical label is added.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: A horizontal line between the horizontal axis and the top of the semicircle meets the graph twice, so the inverse is not a function.

spec.description: Decreasing cosine-shaped segment from the positive vertical axis to a flattening endpoint below the horizontal axis, crossing at the labelled π/2 tick.
spec.mathematics: Only the displayed decreasing segment is reconstructed. Unlabelled endpoint coordinates and vertical values are not asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: Every horizontal line meets the displayed decreasing segment at most once, so its inverse is a function.

spec.description: Three separate increasing tangent-shaped branches, each arrowed at both ends; the central branch passes through the origin.
spec.mathematics: Preserves all three displayed branches without adding numerical ticks or drawn asymptotes. No equation or period is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied decision excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: The horizontal axis meets all three branches. The graph fails the horizontal line test, so the inverse is not a function.
